newsitem.title: USA: Eli Lilly sees new products driving sales.
newsitem.headline: Eli Lilly sees new products driving sales.

text.p: Eli Lilly and Co, which reported higher 1997 first quarter sales and earnings, said Monday new products will fuel sales and expense control will drive profits.

"The introduction of new products and additional indications for existing products will drive our future sales growth," said Randall Tobias, Eli Lilly chairman and chief executive officer, in a statement.
"Our sales growth and strict expense controls helped us realize our first-quarter operating income growth of 21 percent. We will continue to focus on this priority."
Lilly reported first quarter earnings rose 11 percent from a year earlier, to $432.6 million, or $0.79 a share, including a charge of $24 million from termination of an agreement with Somatogen Inc.

Worldwide sales for the first quarter were $1.95 billion, up 10 percent from the first quarter of 1996. Worldwide sales volume growth of 12 percent and a one percent increase in global selling prices were partially offset by unfavorable exchange rate comparisons of three percent, the company said.
The pharmaceutical company said earnings benefited from favorable manufacturing costs and strict expense control.

Worldwide pharmaceutical sales and services for the quarter grew 10 percent, to $1.82 billion. Sales growth was led by three of the company's newer products: Gemzar, a chemotherapy agent for pancreatic cancer; Zyprexa, a treatment for schizophrenia; and ReoPro, which inhibits the formation of blood clots during and after angioplasty in high-risk patients.
In addition, the quarter benefited from increased health-care-management revenues, Lilly said.
Revenue growth was partially offset by lower sales of anti-infectives and lower international sales of Prozac, it said.

Zyprexa, launched in the fourth quarter of 1996, had sales totaling $105.4 million in the first quarter, led by sales in the United States. In March Zyprexa reached a U.S. market share of 10.3 percent of all new antipsychotic prescriptions written, it said.
ReoPro first quarter sales totaled $51.7 million, more than twice the year-ago level.
Gemzar, launched in the U.S. in May 1996, had sales of $33.1 million for the first quarter.
During the first quarter, submissions were filed by Centocor Inc, Lilly's collaboration partner, to expand ReoPro's use in all patients undergoing angioplasty.
Total U.S. pharmaceutical sales and services increased 21 percent in the first quarter from a year earlier, Lilly said.

International pharmaceutical sales fell five percent, with volume growth of six percent being offset by an eight percent unfavorable exchange rate comparison and a three percent reduction in selling prices, Lilly said.
Worldwide sales of animal health products increased one percent, driven by volume growth of four percent, it said.

Manufacturing costs as a percent of sales for the quarter were lower due to a favorable sales mix and increased plant utilization. Marketing and administrative expenses increased only three percent from the first quarter of 1996, largely as a result of cost-control and expense-management programs put in place in the last half of 1996, Lilly said.
Investment in research and development increased nine percent for the quarter, primarily due to clinical trial expenses and increased activities in research collaborations.
